    like most people, im pleasantly surprised about this result and dortmund, the underdog yet somewhat bigger team in this competition, going to the final, but also appalled at the same time by this fact; although this was also supposed to be a mismatch, it must be said that this was a mickey run. the worst team on the other side of the bracket, arsenal, would deal with psg imo. still, that is something more relevant for the format of the competition rather than on an individual team level - any team that gets to a ucl final in big 2024 is pretty good still, and psg and barcelona arent terrible. im waiting for the final matchup to write a proper prediction there, but for now i cannot stop myself from going on a rant about psg. this was your moment to make another ucl final due to the easy run. fine, last 2 years you got madrid and bayern in the r16 or something. (although they weren't great by any means either). now was your easier, final chance 1) with mbappe, and 2) in this ucl format.

    i mention these because, for one, i can only imagine the format from next year being even harder for psg to thrive in. how long will it take now for psg to win the ucl? swiss means, if psg gets good results initially, they are matched up against other good teams in that stage. there will be less easy opponents (relatively), if any. in turn, at the end of swiss, it's hard to imagine psg topping the group ahead of other ucl powerhouses. they'll probably make like top 8 still and have a decent r16, but going forward in the bracket it's not a great seeding. as for the point about mbappe - the dream is over, and in the worst way possible, against a team you were supposed to beat. going to real madrid to win the ucl is like winning with the best car in F1 after always losing with the 2nd best one - definitely a sour taste for me as a fan, at least. i must say, with how high people's expectations of the guy are on twitter, his club career already cannot be nearly as good as cr7 & messi's imo.

    so that dream or ambition for him to be a potential future goat is over. hes younger than cr7 was in 2014, so anything can happen, but how often does a team dominate the ucl as real did between 2014-2018? mbappe's prime as a pacey winger, his main strength, is over within the next couple years - people are already pointing out that his level's dropped since 2022. regardless, he cannot be the versatile focal point as cr7 was, nor can he be the groundbreaking talent that messi was. this goes hand in hand with my next analysis which is psg's weaknesses. as far as mbappe goes, he cannot head, he doesnt score from distance, he cannot dribble in tight spaces, he cannot come up with great passes/crosses. lacking all of these traits, which you might notice ive taken from cr7 & messi, actually make him rather limited - this tie, for one, exposed him further as merely a pace merchant fit only for counterattacks. psg as a whole lacks a bit in creation, and probably a lot of that is on the coach.

    playing such indirect football, a lot of side passes and uninspired decisions that don't take advantage of the players' individual qualities. on psg... oh boy... where do i start. in 2017 it would've been reasonable to say the takeover was recent, and there hadn't been enough time to build the team's structure. it's been 13 years now though. when are we going to see the first psg dynasty such as what city did with pep or even the coaches before that that they trusted way more than psg trusts its coaches? to me, as i always say, it boils down to coaching; sadly the top dogs at psg don't know ball, and much like many of the less-than-intelligent teens on twitter judging teams based on their names on paper, the owners have focused on that rather than trying to see what the better teams are doing behind the scenes. because, to me, when i watch city or madrid these days in high stakes matches, it is clear that they have coaches for everything.

  • [ - ] Icarax - member since 27-Sep-17

    there is a goalkeeper coach, defender coaches etc etc. these teams' players work together on every level, individually and collectively. when psg comes to play, it doesn't seem like the work of a team, but rather a collection of individuals with some vague pointers and basic tactics from the manager. you think donnarumma would be so indecisive on corners, for example, if he played for madrid? that individual issue would've been sorted out ages ago by coaching, not to mention that collective coaching could help reduce such situations as well by having defenders cover for him better. real madrid, the most pretentious team in the world, keeps ancelotti longer even when he doesnt win, than psg keeps its managers - as such, how do you intend to build a dynasty, a structure, a way? it's kind of ironic, because psg has had decent coaches including ancelotti and now enrique, a ucl winner, but they're simply too greedy and want results asap - another way in which they don't know ball.

  • [ - ] Icarax - member since 27-Sep-17

    so my advice is this. don't be greedy, look at how other teams are building: trust managers, and don't undervalue the importance of coaching individually and collectively. don't be shallow and think simply having superstars means they will work together - a mistake many fans make. don't be arrogant and try in any way possible to favor your superstars, build around french players or anything like that - it simply doesn't work (e.g. trusting dembele and barcola is probably a worse choice than looking for other options) or can turn out very costly (e.g. mbappe's contract). know that you are building for the future, and so small apparent sacrifices in the present could turn out beneficial. rant over.
